items.title: Improving Reasoning Capabilities in Small Models through Mixture-of-layers Distillation with Stepwise Attention on Key Information
items.method: Transfers the teacher's stepwise attention to key information with a Mixture-of-Layers alignment module.
items.headline_claim: Consistent gains on math and commonsense reasoning.

items.title: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning
items.method: Pure-RL reasoning (R1-Zero) plus cold-start SFT + RL; 800K R1 samples used for SFT-only distillation into Qwen/Llama 1.5B-70B students.
items.headline_claim: Distilled students beat RL-from-scratch at the same size (e.g. R1-Distill-Qwen-32B > Qwen-32B RL); 'emergent reasoning patterns ... can be systematically used to guide ... smaller models'.
items.path_relevance: Family 3 (reasoning-trace distillation) and family 5 (distilled checkpoints as bases for later RL).
items.frontier_adoption: DeepSeek-R1-Distill models are the standard RL starting point in dozens of 2025-26 papers.

items.title: SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes: A Comparative Study of Foundation Model Post-training
items.affiliations: HKU / UC Berkeley / Google DeepMind / NYU
items.method: Controlled GeneralPoints and V-IRL environments comparing SFT (imitation of traces) with RL on rule and visual variants.
items.headline_claim: RL generalises out-of-distribution while SFT memorises, but SFT is needed to stabilise output format before RL.
items.path_relevance: Family 3/5: evidence on when SFT on traces vs RL generalises and on the 'distill-then-RL' ordering.
items.frontier_adoption: Underpins the SFT-cold-start-then-RL ordering used by DeepSeek-R1, Magistral, Phi-4-reasoning.

items.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling
items.method: SFT of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on 1K curated reasoning traces (Gemini-generated) plus budget forcing.
items.headline_claim: Exceeds o1-preview on MATH/AIME24 by up to 27%; budget forcing extrapolates 50%->57% AIME24.
items.frontier_adoption: None named; widely used as a baseline recipe.

items.title: On Teacher Hacking in Language Model Distillation
items.method: Oracle -> teacher -> student controlled setup; defines teacher hacking (student-teacher distance falls while student-oracle distance rises) and detects it by departure from polynomial convergence.
items.largest_scale: T5-large teacher -> T5-base student (XSum, WMT, NQ)
items.headline_claim: Teacher hacking occurs with fixed offline teacher data; online (teacher- or student-sampled) data or as little as 10% online data removes it; prompt diversity is the key factor.
items.path_relevance: Family 3 (teacher hacking); motivates on-policy/online data in distillation.
items.frontier_adoption: Cited by Residual-Learning KD (ICLR 2026); not named in frontier reports.

items.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview T2TZ0RY4Zk PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at COLM 2025'
items.method: SFT on 817 curated teacher-generated long-CoT examples; 'LIMO hypothesis' that reasoning is latent in pretraining and elicited by few demonstrations.
items.headline_claim: 63.3% AIME24 and 95.6% MATH500 with 1% of prior data; +45.8 pts OOD improvement.

items.title: Distillation Scaling Laws
items.method: Fits a scaling law for student cross-entropy as a function of student size, distillation tokens and teacher cross-entropy; derives compute-optimal teacher/student allocation for 'teacher exists' and 'teacher must be trained' scenarios.
items.largest_scale: Students and teachers 143M-12.6B params, up to 512B tokens
items.headline_claim: Distillation beats supervised pretraining only below a student-size-dependent compute threshold and only when the teacher already exists or is amortised; capacity gap explained as gap in learning capacity, not size; prediction error at most ~1%.
items.path_relevance: Family 6 (theory/compute-optimal teacher selection) and family 4 (distillation pretraining); the primary quantitative statement of a 'distillation ceiling' in pretraining.
items.frontier_adoption: Cited by the OPD survey (2604.00626) as the only distillation scaling law; Apple AFM 2025 uses distillation pretraining.

items.title: Small Models Struggle to Learn from Strong Reasoners
items.method: Studies long- vs short-CoT and large- vs small-teacher distillation into <=3B students; proposes Mix Distillation.
items.headline_claim: Small Model Learnability Gap: <=3B students do not consistently benefit from long CoT or large teachers; mixing long/short CoT recovers performance.

items.title: Unveiling the Key Factors for Distilling Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.affiliations: HK PolyU / EIT Ningbo / Saarland / Meituan
items.method: 4 teachers x 7 students x 7 datasets ablating CoT granularity, format and teacher strength.
items.headline_claim: Stronger teachers do not always produce better students; SLMs show non-monotonic response to CoT granularity.

items.title: DistiLLM-2: A Contrastive Approach Boosts the Distillation of LLMs
items.method: Contrastive objective: increase likelihood of teacher responses and decrease likelihood of student responses, pairing loss form with data type (teacher- vs student-generated).
items.headline_claim: Outperforms DistiLLM/GKD-style baselines on instruction following and code; extends to preference alignment and VLMs.

items.title: Universal Cross-Tokenizer Distillation via Approximate Likelihood Matching
items.method: Approximate likelihood matching over chunk alignments so distillation works across fundamentally different tokenizers (incl. subword->byte).
items.headline_claim: First effective distillation across fundamentally different tokenizers; distils a maths-specialised LLM into a general model with a different tokenizer.
items.frontier_adoption: None named; SimCT (2605.07711) extends to on-policy.

items.title: Minitron-SSM: Efficient Hybrid Language Model Compression through Group-Aware SSM Pruning
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview m3huAdsaGI listed as NeurIPS 2025; NVlabs/Minitron README: 'Accepted to NeurIPS 2025'
items.method: Group-aware Mamba/SSM pruning plus FFN/embedding/depth pruning, then logit (forward-KL) distillation from the unpruned teacher.
items.headline_claim: 50% size reduction retaining >96% accuracy with up to 40x fewer tokens; ~2x faster inference.

items.title: OpenThoughts: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models
items.affiliations: Stanford / UW / Bespoke Labs / TRI / Berkeley
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview fNh86fMBxS PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'
items.method: 1,000+ controlled experiments on prompt sourcing, filtering, teacher choice and scale for SFT-based reasoning distillation; OpenThoughts3-1.2M with QwQ-32B teacher.
items.headline_claim: OpenThinker2-32B first public-data model to match R1-Distill-32B; OpenThoughts3-7B 53% AIME25 / 51% LiveCodeBench.
items.frontier_adoption: Used as the off-policy cold-start dataset in Thinking Machines' OPD study and in Magistral Small cold start.

items.title: Distillation of Large Language Models via Concrete Score Matching
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview bZBJFrxH1H PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'; github aailab-kaist/CSD '[ICLR 2026]'
items.method: Concrete Score Distillation: matches pairwise logit residuals f[x]-f[y] between student and teacher (shift-invariant, linear-time gradient), with mode-seeking or mode-covering weightings.
items.largest_scale: Teachers up to Gemma2-9B-IT; students GPT-2 1.5B to 7B
items.headline_claim: Consistently surpasses KL-family and direct-logit objectives; complementary to on-policy techniques.

items.title: Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models through Residual Learning
items.method: Two-stage white-box KD: compress teacher hidden states via self-reconstruction projectors, then residual learning on teacher-error tokens; expert fusion for MoE teachers and cross-model attention for cross-tokenizer pairs.
items.headline_claim: Best average Rouge-L in same- and cross-tokenizer settings; MoE-teacher expert fusion.

items.title: Theoretical Perspectives on Knowledge Distillation: A Review
items.tier_evidence: Wiley WIREs Computational Statistics, published 08 Oct 2025 (Scholar Gateway record)
items.method: Review of theoretical accounts of why distillation works.
items.headline_claim: Survey of KD theory.

items.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
items.method: OPSD: same model as teacher (conditioned on privileged ground-truth solution) and student (question only); per-token reverse KL on student rollouts.
items.headline_claim: 4-8x token efficiency vs GRPO; beats off-policy distillation on math benchmarks.
items.frontier_adoption: Privileged self-distillation variants adopted in several 2026 follow-ups; no frontier report yet.

items.title: Privileged Information Distillation for Language Models (pi-Distill)
items.method: Shared-parameter PI-conditioned teacher and unconditioned student trained jointly; also an OPSD variant with reverse-KL penalty.
items.headline_claim: pi-Distill (and sometimes OPSD) beats SFT-then-RL pipelines that assume full CoT access, using action-only privileged information.

items.title: Pedagogically-Inspired Data Synthesis for Language Model Knowledge Distillation
items.method: Identifier-Organizer-Adapter pipeline that diagnoses student deficiencies and synthesises teacher data progressively.
items.headline_claim: Improves over one-shot synthetic-data distillation.

items.title: Entropy-Aware On-Policy Distillation of Language Models
items.method: EOPD: reverse KL on low-entropy teacher tokens, forward KL (over teacher top-k) where teacher entropy > tau, preserving diversity.
items.headline_claim: Pass@8 +1.37 / +2.39 / +5.05 over standard OPD across six math benchmarks.

items.title: Revisiting On-Policy Distillation: Empirical Failure Modes and Simple Fixes
items.method: Analyses sampled-token reverse-KL OPD: token-level estimator is biased vs sequence-level reverse KL but has tighter variance; identifies three failure modes (imbalanced one-token signal, unreliable teacher on student prefixes, length distortion) and simple fixes.
items.headline_claim: Fixes recover OPD in long-horizon settings where the sampled-token variant collapses.
items.path_relevance: Family 1/6 (OPD estimator theory and failure modes).

items.title: Gemma 3 Technical Report
items.method: All models pretrained with knowledge distillation (256 sampled teacher logits per token, renormalised); post-training uses improved KD from a large IT teacher plus BOND/WARM/WARP RL.
items.headline_claim: Gemma3-27B-IT comparable to Gemini-1.5-Pro; ablation: smaller teacher better for short horizons, larger teacher better for long horizons.
items.path_relevance: Family 4 (distillation from Gemini as primary route; distilled bases then RL).
items.frontier_adoption: Gemma 3; Gemma 3n reuses architecture (blog discloses distillation only for the MobileNet-V5 vision encoder).

items.title: The Llama 4 herd (blog)
items.tier_evidence: Meta launch blog (no technical report published)
items.method: Codistillation of Llama 4 Maverick from the ~2T-parameter Behemoth teacher during pretraining with a loss that dynamically weights soft and hard targets; teacher forward passes amortised across student data.
items.largest_scale: Teacher ~2T total / 288B active; student Maverick 400B/17B active
items.headline_claim: 'We codistilled the Llama 4 Maverick model from Llama 4 Behemoth ... resulting in substantial quality improvements'.

items.title: Phi-4-reasoning Technical Report
items.method: SFT of Phi-4 (14B) on 1.4M prompts with o3-mini-generated long CoT traces (16B tokens), then short outcome-based RL (Phi-4-reasoning-plus).
items.headline_claim: Outperforms R1-Distill-Llama-70B; o3-mini-high a stronger teacher than medium; RL on top adds accuracy at 1.5x tokens.

items.title: Llama-Nemotron: Efficient Reasoning Models
items.tier_evidence: NVIDIA technical report on arXiv; OpenReview ev1xpo9mbI (EXAIT@ICML 2025 workshop)
items.method: NAS + knowledge distillation (Puzzle) from Llama-3 teachers, then reasoning SFT on DeepSeek-R1 traces and large-scale RL.
items.headline_claim: Ultra matches/exceeds R1 with higher throughput.
items.path_relevance: Family 4/5 (pruning-plus-distillation base then SFT and RL).

items.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
items.method: Strong-to-weak distillation for 0.6B-14B dense and 30B-A3B MoE: off-policy distillation on teacher /think and /no_think outputs, then on-policy distillation minimising KL to Qwen3-32B or Qwen3-235B-A22B logits on student rollouts.
items.headline_claim: Distillation 'achieves significantly better performance than reinforcement learning while requiring approximately only 1/10 of the GPU hours' and raises pass@64, which RL did not.
items.frontier_adoption: Qwen3; replicated by Thinking Machines; cited by GLM-5, MiMo, Nemotron.

items.title: Magistral
items.method: Magistral Medium via pure RLVR (no distillation); Magistral Small 24B cold-started by SFT on Magistral Medium traces then RL.
items.headline_claim: SFT+RL best; contrary to DeepSeek-R1, pure RL on a 24B base matches distillation on AIME24, and RL on top of the distilled checkpoint adds >5 points.
items.path_relevance: Family 5 (distilled checkpoint as RL starting point; ordering evidence).

items.title: Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models: Tech Report 2025
items.method: On-device ~3B model: train dense 14T tokens, sparse-upcycle to 64-expert MoE on 1T tokens, then retrain the dense model on the last 10% (1.4T) tokens with a distillation loss from the MoE teacher.
items.largest_scale: ~3B on-device student; PT-MoE server model 14T tokens
items.headline_claim: Pipeline 'reduced the cost of training the large distillation teacher by 90%' and improved the pretrained on-device model; no structural pruning needed.
items.path_relevance: Family 4/5 (distillation as pretraining finish and the distilled model then goes to SFT+RL).
items.frontier_adoption: Apple Foundation Models 2025; AFM 3 (June 2026 blog) discloses SFT + multi-stage RL and QAT but no distillation detail yet.

items.title: On-Policy Distillation (Thinking Machines Lab: Connectionism)
items.method: Student samples trajectories; teacher grades every token with per-token reverse KL used as a dense advantage in an RL loop; implemented in Tinker.
items.largest_scale: Qwen3-8B-Base student, Qwen3-32B teacher; also personalization on an internal assistant
items.headline_claim: 70% AIME'24 in ~150 steps from a 400K-SFT checkpoint; 9-30x cheaper than off-policy distillation and 7-10x fewer gradient steps (50-100x compute) than RL; recovers instruction following lost during mid-training.
items.path_relevance: Family 1 (the canonical OPD write-up cited by Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4, Nemotron, GLM-5).
items.frontier_adoption: Cited as reference recipe by Kimi K3 [75], DeepSeek-V4, Nemotron 3 Ultra, Nemotron-Cascade 2, MiMo.

items.title: DeepSeek-V3.2: Pushing the Frontier of Open Large Language Models
items.method: Specialist distillation: six RL-trained domain specialists generate data for the final checkpoint (off-policy), followed by mixed RL.
items.headline_claim: 'models trained on the distilled data achieve performance levels only marginally below those of domain-specific specialists, with the performance gap being effectively eliminated through subsequent RL training'.
items.path_relevance: Family 3/5 (off-policy specialist distillation then RL ordering).

items.title: MiMo-V2-Flash Technical Report
items.first_author_et_al: Xiaomi MiMo Core Team (Xia et al.)
items.method: MOPD: SFT -> independently RL-trained domain teachers -> student learns from dense token-level KL rewards from domain teachers plus a verifiable outcome reward.
items.headline_claim: 'MOPD preserves peak performance of the strongest teacher across all domains'; rivals DeepSeek-V3.2 and Kimi-K2 with 1/2-1/3 the parameters.
items.frontier_adoption: MiMo-V2-Flash; cited by Kimi K3, Nemotron 3 Ultra, Nemotron-Cascade 2.

items.title: Kimi K2.5: Visual Agentic Intelligence
items.method: SFT data 'synthesizing high-quality candidate responses from K2, K2 Thinking and a suite of proprietary in-house expert models' (off-policy teacher-generated data), then joint text-vision RL and PARL; the word 'distillation' does not appear in the report.
items.headline_claim: No explicit distillation stage disclosed; expert-generated SFT data is the only teacher-derived signal.
items.path_relevance: Family 4 (check of frontier disclosure): K2.5 does not disclose OPD; K3 does.

items.title: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
items.method: On-Policy Cross-Stage Distillation as the final post-training stage: checkpoints from earlier SFT/Reasoning-RL/General-RL stages act as teachers; advantage term of the GRPO loss replaced by the teacher-student log-ratio; GRPO group size 1, batch 1024; teacher logits fetched from the inference engine.
items.headline_claim: 'we perform on-policy cross-stage distillation as the final stage ... to swiftly recover the skills acquired in earlier SFT and RL stages'; mitigates capability regression across sequential RL stages.
items.path_relevance: Family 1 (OPD variant used to fight forgetting).
items.frontier_adoption: GLM-5; extended in GLM-5.2 to parallel multi-expert OPD.

items.title: Nemotron-Cascade 2: Post-Training LLMs with Cascade RL and Multi-Domain On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Multi-domain OPD inserted inside Cascade RL: teachers are the strongest intermediate checkpoints per domain; reverse-KL token advantage with truncated importance weights.
items.headline_claim: MOPD reaches 92.0 AIME25 in 30 steps vs GRPO 91.0 after 25; recovers regressions from earlier RL stages; IMO/IOI/ICPC gold.
items.path_relevance: Family 1/5 (OPD as stabiliser inside an RL cascade).

items.title: Qwen3.5-Omni Technical Report
items.method: Stage 1 specialist distillation (domain teachers fine-tuned from the Qwen-3.5 base, incl. vision/audio teachers) then Stage 2 on-policy distillation of the model's text-conditioned responses into its audio-conditioned behaviour, then interaction RL.
items.headline_claim: Specialist distillation plus OPD closes the audio-vs-text response-quality gap.
items.path_relevance: Family 1 (cross-modal OPD; distilled model as base for RL).

items.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
items.v1_date: 2026-04-26 (abs page date; arXiv id in 2606 series)
items.method: Two-stage post-training: per-domain SFT+GRPO specialists (math, code, agent, IF, ...) then a unified student trained by full-vocabulary on-policy distillation with reverse-KL loss against the teachers; 'Efficient Teacher Scheduling for Full-Vocabulary OPD' infrastructure section.
items.largest_scale: V4-Pro 1.6T/49B active and V4-Flash 284B/13B active; 32-33T pretraining tokens
items.headline_claim: 'a single unified model is trained through on-policy distillation, wherein the unified model acts as the student learning to optimize the reverse KL loss with teacher models'.
items.path_relevance: Family 1/5 (OPD as the frontier consolidation route).
items.frontier_adoption: DeepSeek-V4; cited by Kimi K3 as MOPD precedent.

items.title: Nemotron 3 Ultra: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
items.tier_evidence: NVIDIA technical report on arXiv (and research.nvidia.com PDF)
items.method: SFT -> RLVR -> one-time 'MOPD warmup' SFT -> asynchronous MOPD from >10 domain teachers over two iterations with teacher co-evolution; head-only KL distillation for MTP drafts.
items.headline_claim: 'more than ten domain-specialized teacher models ... MOPD consolidated these teachers into Ultra through dense token-level guidance on student-generated rollouts'.
items.path_relevance: Family 1/4/5 (iterative MOPD at frontier scale; distilled student re-used as teacher init).

items.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks (blog)
items.tier_evidence: Lab blog post dated 2026-06-16; no separate tech report (model card cites the GLM-5 report)
items.method: Parallel on-policy distillation in the slime framework merging >10 independently RL-trained expert models into the final model.
items.headline_claim: 'we used the slime framework to conduct parallel OPD training, efficiently merging more than ten expert models into the final model. The entire OPD training process took approximately two days'.
items.path_relevance: Family 1/5 (multi-expert OPD consolidation at frontier scale).

items.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
items.method: SFT -> domain- and effort-specialised RL experts (nine teachers over 3 effort levels) -> Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) with clipped per-token log-ratio reward r = clip(sg(log pi_teacher/pi_theta), -Rmax, Rmax).
items.headline_claim: 'Domain- and effort-specialized policies are consolidated into a unified model through multi-teacher on-policy distillation [75, 135, 29]'; 'we also experimented with more fine-grained top-k distillation objectives, we observed no clear advantage'.
items.path_relevance: Family 1/5: frontier-scale MOPD as the final consolidation stage; explicit disclosure of distillation in the recipe.
items.frontier_adoption: Kimi K3 itself; cites Thinking Machines OPD [75], MiMo-V2-Flash [135], DeepSeek-V4 [29].

items.title: Sky-T1: Train your own O1 preview model within $450 (blog)
items.method: SFT of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on 17K rejection-sampled QwQ-32B-Preview traces reformatted by GPT-4o-mini.
items.headline_claim: On par with o1-preview on math/coding (AIME24 43.3).

items.title: Every Expert Matters: Towards Effective Knowledge Distillation for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
items.method: MoE-specific KD (knowledge augmentation, student-aware router) exploiting non-activated experts.
items.headline_claim: Non-activated experts carry useful knowledge; standard KD is suboptimal for MoE teachers.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning vs. Distillation: Understanding Accuracy and Capability in LLM Reasoning
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview submission page exists; no accepted venue found
items.method: Disentangles reasoning patterns from new knowledge in teacher traces via controlled distillation.
items.headline_claim: Distillation raises capability (pass@k) only when it introduces new knowledge; pattern-only distillation behaves like RLVR.
items.path_relevance: Family 3/5 (when SFT on traces beats RL).

items.title: RLKD: Distilling LLMs' Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
items.method: RL-based distillation of the implicit multi-branch structure of teacher reasoning.
items.headline_claim: Beats SFT trace distillation on reasoning.

items.title: Language Model Distillation: A Temporal Difference Imitation Learning Perspective
items.method: Casts LM distillation as inverse RL / TD imitation learning with a reduced action space.
items.headline_claim: Provides a TD-learning framing that subsumes behaviour-cloning-style distillation.

items.title: Why Distillation can Outperform Zero-RL: The Role of Flexible Reasoning
items.method: Distils 920 examples into a base model and compares with zero-RL, analysing token usage.
items.headline_claim: Distillation with 920 examples beats zero-RL; distilled models show more multi-perspective and metacognitive tokens.

items.title: SlimMoE: Structured Compression of Large MoE Models via Expert Slimming and Distillation
items.method: Multi-stage expert slimming with intermediate distillation stages.
items.headline_claim: Compresses MoE into smaller MoE without one-shot pruning loss.

items.title: Rethinking Large Language Model Distillation: A Constrained Markov Decision Process Perspective
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview TBJIf2M23q: 'ICLR 2026 Conference Withdrawn Submission' (reviews exist)
items.method: Reward-aware distillation as constrained RL: maximise task reward subject to a KL-to-teacher budget via a modified Saute reward without state augmentation.
items.headline_claim: Better constraint satisfaction than Lagrangian relaxations at competitive accuracy.

items.title: Stable On-Policy Distillation through Adaptive Target Reformulation
items.method: Veto: geometric bridge target in logit space between teacher and student.
items.headline_claim: Avoids pathological forward-KL gradients and reverse-KL diversity collapse.

items.title: Which Reasoning Trajectories Teach Students to Reason Better? A Simple Metric of Informative Alignment
items.method: Metric for selecting teacher trajectories for distillation.
items.headline_claim: Informative-alignment metric predicts student gains.

items.title: Memorization Dynamics in Knowledge Distillation for Language Models
items.method: Measures training-data memorisation transfer through KD.
items.headline_claim: KD as a privacy mechanism has measurable leakage dynamics.

items.title: Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward Extrapolation
items.method: Proves OPD is a special case of dense KL-constrained RL with equal reward/KL weight; G-OPD adds a reference model and reward scale; ExOPD (scale >1) and reward correction with the teacher's pre-RL base.
items.headline_claim: ExOPD lets a student surpass its domain teachers when merging RL experts back into the base.
items.path_relevance: Family 6 (dense-reward interpretation of OPD) and family 1.

items.title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models
items.method: OPCD: reverse KL to a context-conditioned teacher on the student's own rollouts to internalise in-context knowledge / system prompts.
items.headline_claim: Beats context-distillation baselines and preserves OOD ability; supports cross-size distillation.

items.title: Fast and Effective On-policy Distillation from Reasoning Prefixes
items.method: Distils only on short teacher prefixes where OPD signal concentrates, cutting rollout cost.
items.headline_claim: Prefix-only OPD matches full OPD at lower cost.

items.title: Scaling Reasoning Efficiently via Relaxed On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Relaxed OPD for small reasoning models where direct reward RL fails.
items.headline_claim: Competitive with ProRL/DeepScaleR on AIME25.

items.title: A Survey of On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Models
items.method: Unified f-divergence framework over on-policy samples; taxonomy by feedback signal, teacher access and loss granularity; industrial deployment section and open problems.
items.headline_claim: First comprehensive OPD survey; lists Qwen3, MiMo-V2-Flash, KAT-Coder-V2, Nemotron-Cascade 2, DeepSeek-V4 as industrial adopters.
items.path_relevance: Snowball seed and survey for family 1.

items.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
items.method: Systematic OPD dynamics study: two success conditions (thinking-pattern consistency; teacher offers genuinely new knowledge), overlap-token mechanism, off-policy cold start and teacher-aligned prompts as fixes.
items.headline_claim: A weaker 1.5B teacher (JustRL) improves the student where a stronger R1-Distill-7B teacher fails; overlap tokens carry 97-99% of mass; dense reward degrades over long trajectories.
items.frontier_adoption: None named; cites Qwen3, MiMo, GLM-5 as adopters.

items.title: The Illusion of Certainty: Decoupling Capability and Calibration in On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Identifies a 'Scaling Law of Miscalibration' under privileged-context OPD and proposes CaOPD (student-grounded confidence targets).
items.headline_claim: OPD drives mean confidence to ~0.996; CaOPD collapses the overconfidence gap without a capability tax.

items.title: OPSDL: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Context Language Models
items.method: Uses the model's own short-context ability as self-teacher for long-context OPD.
items.headline_claim: Improves long-context without privileged data.

items.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation: Bridging Exploitation and Imitation at the Token Level
items.method: Replaces negative reinforcement in non-positive-advantage regions with localised divergence minimisation.
items.headline_claim: Fixes high variance, vanishing gradients and exploration bottlenecks of advantage-weighted OPD.

items.title: SimCT: Recovering Lost Supervision for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Recovers teacher signal lost by exact shared-token matching when teacher and student tokenise differently.
items.headline_claim: Enables cross-tokenizer OPD.

items.title: KL for a KL: On-Policy Distillation with Control Variate Baseline
items.method: vOPD: control-variate baseline whose value function is the closed-form per-token negative reverse KL.
items.headline_claim: Stabilises single-sample OPD.

items.title: Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training
items.method: Reward-density principle: spend sparse verifiable rewards on a model where exploration is productive (a larger teacher), then compress with dense OPD into the deployment student.
items.headline_claim: GRPO-on-teacher then OPD beats GRPO directly on the student under fixed labelled-data budget.
items.path_relevance: Family 5/6 (when to RL and when to distil).

items.title: Prefix Teach, Suffix Fade: Local Teachability Collapse in Strong-to-Weak On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Shows later trajectory segments keep a non-zero advantage but lose local contrast, so dense feedback stops being actionable.
items.headline_claim: Full-sequence supervision does not monotonically help in strong-to-weak OPD.

items.title: Decoupling KL and Trajectories: A Unified Perspective for SFT, DAgger, Offline RL, and OPD in LLM Distillation
items.affiliations: EIT Ningbo / HK PolyU / SJTU / HKUST(GZ)
items.method: Decomposes sequence-level KL to show off-policy vs on-policy distillation couple prefix source and KL direction; explores the decoupled 2x2 design space.
items.headline_claim: Prefix source and KL direction are orthogonal choices.

items.title: Self-Supervised On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning Language Models
items.method: Distils a teacher conditioned on the shortest correct completion into prefixes of the longest wrong completion within a GRPO group.
items.headline_claim: Dense process supervision without external traces.

items.title: Strong Teacher Not Needed? On Distillation in LLM Pretraining
items.method: Varies teacher/student sizes (0.7B-8B) in distillation pretraining.
items.headline_claim: Weak-to-strong and same-level teachers help (+0.7 to +3.4%); an overly strong teacher saturates and underperforms a compatible one.

items.title: Pruning and Distilling Mixture-of-Experts into Dense Language Models
items.method: Score, select, group and concatenate experts into a dense FFN, then distil from the MoE teacher; 350 configurations.
items.headline_claim: MoE-to-dense beats dense-to-dense pruning by +6.3 pp at matched size with 1.6x faster training.

items.title: A Predictive Law for On-Policy Self-Distillation From World Feedback
items.method: Empirical law: final OPSD gain is linear in the initial student/self-teacher gap.
items.headline_claim: Linear predictability holds across context types and scales.

items.title: Bridging Reasoning Trajectories in On-Policy Distillation via Near-Future Guidance
items.method: TOPD uses near-future trajectory information to find real divergence points instead of surface-form high-loss tokens.
items.headline_claim: ~30% of high-loss tokens are surface mismatches, not reasoning forks.

items.title: Filter, Then Reweight: Rethinking Optimization Granularity in On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Trajectory filtering followed by soft token reweighting (FiRe-OPD).
items.headline_claim: Beats hard token selection.

items.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Parameter-space diagnostics comparing OPD, SFT and RLVR update trajectories.
items.headline_claim: OPD lies in a 'relaxed off-principal regime': touches fewer weights and avoids principal directions more than SFT, but is less constrained than RLVR.

items.title: On the Position Bias of On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Shows teacher supervision degrades with rollout position; derives importance-weighted OPD from a constrained-optimisation view.
items.headline_claim: First 30% of tokens alone match full-sequence OPD; last 30% alone 'barely learns anything'.

items.title: A Formula-Driven Survey and Research Agenda for On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Taxonomy of OPD as a feedback-to-update problem: direct distributional losses vs policy-gradient log-ratio updates; covers hybrids with verifiers and industrial recipes.
items.headline_claim: Frames OPD stability (unreliable, support-truncated, poorly credited feedback) as the central design problem.

items.title: Finding the Evidence: Discovering Decision-Supporting Tokens for On-Policy Reasoning Distillation
items.method: Separates decision tokens (student uncertainty) from evidence tokens (student confident but wrong) in OPD.
items.headline_claim: Current OPD captures only decision tokens.

items.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
items.tier_evidence: ICML 2026 RLxF workshop poster (icml.cc/virtual/2026/78170), not main track; arXiv preprint
items.method: Controlled MOPD study: per-domain RL teachers from the same SFT checkpoint, per-prompt routing, per-token reverse KL (policy-gradient or top-k form).
items.headline_claim: Beats Mix-RL, Cascade RL, Off-Policy Finetune and Param-Merge by 5.5 normalised points, closing 91-95% of teacher headroom; cross-family teacher (Qwen3-235B) collapses training.

items.title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
items.method: Advantage-aware routing of token supervision between a privileged teacher and a privileged student to avoid 'privilege illusion'.
items.headline_claim: Outperforms single-source OPD/OPSD on LLM and VLM reasoning.

items.title: Behavior Cloning is Not All You Need: The Optimality of On-Policy Distillation for Noisy Expert Feedback
items.method: Noisy-expert imitation-learning model; proves offline IL needs sample complexity exponential in horizon to match a clean expert while an OPD variant achieves polynomial dependence.
items.headline_claim: Sharp offline/online separation explaining why OPD beats SFT when the teacher is imperfect.
items.path_relevance: Family 6 (sample-complexity theory of distillation vs SFT/RL).

items.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Direct-OPD: uses log(pi_post-RL-weak / pi_pre-RL-weak) as a dense implicit reward on the stronger student's own rollouts.
items.largest_scale: Weak teachers <=1.7B, students up to Qwen3-8B
items.headline_claim: Boosts Qwen3-1.7B from 48.3% to 58.3% on AIME; weaker RL'd teachers consistently improve stronger students.

items.title: Rethinking On-Policy Self-Distillation for Thinking Models
items.method: Evaluates privileged-context self-distillation on thinking models at long rollout budgets.
items.largest_scale: Five Qwen3 and OLMo thinking models
items.headline_claim: Privileged self-distillation causes up to 17% relative drop in avg@16 on AIME/HMMT; degradation grows with withheld context.

items.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Roles, Pathologies, and Regulations
items.method: Positions OPD as an exploration catalyst; identifies student-teacher mismatch and length exploitation; proposes advantage clipping and log-scale compression.
items.headline_claim: Regulated OPD beats OPD variants and RLVR; 'well-regulated signal quality, rather than mere teacher scale, governs successful exploration'.

items.title: Distilled Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-training
items.method: Integrates teacher supervision into the RL objective via reverse importance sampling with clipping, negative-sample reset and sequence-level geometric normalisation.
items.headline_claim: Beats RL and OPD on pass@1 and pass@k in within- and cross-family settings; argues plain OPD is 'largely restricted to within-family distillation'.

items.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling
items.method: Pass@K / avg@K analysis up to K=1024 across OPD variants and teachers.
items.headline_claim: 'Illusory distillation': OPD improves avg@K but the pass@K boundary at K=1024 never exceeds the pre-OPD base, unlike off-policy distillation which expands it.

items.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Controlled M-OPD benchmark with oracle routing; token-share balancing, gap-aware budget allocation, student reward refresh.
items.headline_claim: Standard M-OPD captures only 35.6% of oracle headroom; Open-MOPD raises it to 83.4%.
items.frontier_adoption: None; reproduces the frontier MOPD pattern openly.

items.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
items.method: Combines RLVR outcome rewards with OPD token rewards.
items.headline_claim: Hybrid beats either alone.

items.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.method: Critical review of OPSD (self-teacher with privileged information).
items.headline_claim: Argues OPSD's teacher is no stronger than the student and analyses three levers governing its gains.

items.title: A Token-Level Analysis of Sampled-Token Reverse-KL On-Policy Distillation
items.method: Gradient analysis of the K2 reverse-KL estimator: update norm factorises into the teacher-student log-prob gap and a student softmax factor.
items.headline_claim: Explains why sampled-token OPD over-weights tokens the student finds unlikely.

items.title: Compact Language Models via Pruning and Knowledge Distillation (Minitron) [BASELINE, v1 2024-07, out of window]
items.method: Structured pruning plus KL distillation retraining.
items.headline_claim: Up to 40x fewer tokens; best-practice list including 'retrain exclusively with distillation loss'.

items.title: Speculative Knowledge Distillation: Bridging the Teacher-Student Gap Through Interleaved Sampling [BASELINE, v1 2024-10, out of window]
items.method: Student proposes tokens, teacher replaces those outside its top-K (speculative-decoding style), interpolating supervised and on-policy KD.
items.headline_claim: Beats supervised and on-policy KD across translation, summarisation, math.

open_problems.statement: Distillation scaling laws for OPD: 'no equivalent framework exists for on-policy distillation, where the generation cost of student rollouts introduces an additional compute axis'; key question 'whether more on-policy data can compensate for a weaker teacher, or whether teacher quality sets a hard ceiling regardless of rollout volume'.

Agent-level distillation: 'the systematic degradation of teacher supervision with trajectory depth ... remains a challenging open problem'; uncertainty-aware feedback ('teachers currently supply point-estimate probabilities') is listed as a second foundational gap.

'OPD's apparent free lunch of dense token-level reward comes at a cost, raising the question of whether OPD can scale to long-horizon distillation'; future work proposes hybrids of dense token supervision on short segments with sparse outcome rewards for long horizons.
Whether OPD transfers new capability at all: at K=1024 'OPD-trained models do not exceed their pre-OPD base models', so capability expansion from a stronger teacher through OPD is untested at scale.

Cross-family distillation: MOPD with a Qwen3-235B teacher 'diverges catastrophically'; Distilled RL states plain OPD is 'largely restricting OPD to within-family distillation'. No frontier report distils across model families.
'open, rigorously reproducible recipes are conspicuously lacking' for multi-teacher OPD; standard M-OPD recovers only 35.6% of oracle headroom.

Distillation 'can not produce lower model cross-entropies than supervised learning when both learning processes are given enough data or compute'; the compute threshold beyond which distillation stops paying is student-size dependent and has not been measured at >12.6B scale.

Infrastructure: 'Currently, we utilize the inference engine to fetch teachers' logits. In the future, we plan to migrate the inference backend to the training engine' (train/infer logit mismatch in OPD).
Kimi K3 found 'no clear advantage' for top-k distillation objectives over sampled-token OPD 'in our setting'; the objective choice at trillion-parameter scale is unresolved.
'capability distillation does not imply calibrated confidence'; OPD under privileged context produces a 'Scaling Law of Miscalibration'.

Nemotron 3 Ultra needs a 'MOPD warmup' SFT to align student rollouts with teacher-supported distributions and runs two MOPD iterations; how many iterations of teacher co-evolution help, and the cost of retraining >10 teachers per iteration, are not analysed.

In pretraining distillation 'an overly strong teacher can overwhelm the student'; teacher-student compatibility rather than teacher strength governs gains, with no rule for choosing the compatible teacher at scale.

A Formula-Driven Survey and Research Agenda for On-Policy Distillation (Zhang, Tsinghua, 2026-06-22)

Theoretical Perspectives on Knowledge Distillation: A Review (WIREs Computational Statistics, Wiley, 2025-10-08)
Industrial-deployment table in the OPD survey lists Qwen3, Gemma 2, MiMo-V2-Flash, KAT-Coder-V2, Nemotron-Cascade 2, DeepSeek-V4, ORBIT as OPD/KD adopters

negative_results.statement: Kimi K3: fine-grained top-k OPD objectives gave 'no clear advantage in either convergence speed or final performance' over the clipped sampled-token log-ratio reward.

MOPD: distilling from a cross-family Qwen3-235B-A22B teacher degrades math accuracy under the policy-gradient loss and 'diverges catastrophically around step 18' under top-k; same-origin teachers are required.

A stronger teacher (R1-Distill-7B) 'fails to yield any improvement' where a weaker JustRL-1.5B teacher recovers >80% of the gap; same-family 1.5B and 7B teachers are 'distributionally indistinguishable from the student's perspective'.
OPD improves avg@K but never expands the pass@1024 boundary; more previously solvable problems become unsolvable than the reverse ('illusory distillation').
Privileged self-distillation degrades thinking models by up to 17% relative avg@16 on AIME24/25 and HMMT25.
Standard OPD (SDFT/SDPO) drives confidence to ~0.996 and worsens overconfidence across settings.
Students <=3B do not consistently benefit from long CoT or large teachers (Small Model Learnability Gap).
Stronger teachers do not always produce better students in CoT distillation.
Very-strong-to-weak pretraining distillation (8B -> 1.7B) underperforms a compatible 3.8B teacher.
Offline distillation on a fixed teacher dataset exhibits teacher hacking; only online data or prompt diversity prevents it.
Distillation never beats supervised pretraining at sufficient compute; if the teacher must be trained for a single student, supervised learning wins.
Teacher signal on later rollout positions is nearly useless (last 30% of tokens 'barely learns anything'); local teachability collapses in strong-to-weak OPD.
Vanilla multi-teacher OPD recovers only 35.6% of oracle ensemble headroom, with instruction following degrading.
Magistral contradicts DeepSeek-R1's small-model claim: pure RL on a 24B base matches distillation on AIME24, although RL on top of the distilled checkpoint is best.
Gemma 3 ablation: for short training horizons the smaller teacher is better; the trend reverses only for long horizons.
Length exploitation (truncation or padding) and unreliable teacher guidance on student prefixes are recurrent OPD failure modes.
Kimi K2.5 discloses no distillation stage (only SFT on data synthesised from K2/K2-Thinking/in-house experts), so the K2.5 recipe offers no evidence for or against OPD.
